answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock a refundable bond before bidding, then use random audits to check whether its claimed work is valid; proven fraud burns the bond and excludes the account. Because influence and access depend on bonded value rather than account count, splitting funds across a hundred names does not multiply power. A sybil attacker must commit more capital for more reach and risk losing it, while honest agents recover their bonds. Even across mesa, echo, and tundra markets, the same rule applies.
